content: 1. The coadministration of polatuzumab vedotin with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, such as darunavir, may increase the area under the curve (AUC) of unconjugated monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), potentially leading to increased toxicities associated with polatuzumab vedotin. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, MMAE, and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a substrate of CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Monitor for increased adverse reactions to darunavir or cobicistat. 4. Darunavir decreases the effects of pramlintide through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Darunavir increases pravastatin levels through an unknown mechanism, likely involving CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Similarly, cobicistat increases pravastatin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 6. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of praziquantel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of prednisolone and prednisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, prednisone decreases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of primaquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Primidone decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of progesterone (intravaginal gel, micronized, and natural forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with antiarrhythmics. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of protriptyline by mechanisms involving CYP3A4 inhibition. Carefully titrate the dose of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitor its response during coadministration. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of quazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Quinidine is a substrate of CYP3A4 and P-gp and inhibits CYP2D6 and P-gp. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Cobicistat and darunavir increase the levels or effects of quizartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce the quizartinib dose to 4 mg/day when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the pre-inhibitor dose after discontinuation of the strong inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of rabeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce the rifabutin dose to 150 mg orally every other day and monitor for associated adverse reactions such as neutropenia and uveitis. 22. Rifapentine decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Darunavir increases rifaximin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Cobicistat and darunavir increase the levels or effects of ripretinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 25. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of risperidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be required upon coadministration. 26. Darunavir increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both darunavir and ritonavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Darunavir increases rivaroxaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use of rivaroxaban with known combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 28. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of roflumilast (oral and topical) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Darunavir increases ropivacaine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Darunavir decreases the effects of rosiglitazone through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 32. Darunavir and cobicistat increase rosuvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, the dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. 33. Rucaparib increases cobicistat and darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 34. Rufinamide decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 35. Cobicistat increases seladelpar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Monitor for adverse effects if coadministered with BCRP inhibitors. 36. Darunavir increases saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce the saxagliptin dose to 5 mg/day when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 37. Cobicistat increases selexipag levels by inhibiting ABCG2 (BCRP) transporters. Monitor for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects when coadministered with BCRP inhibitors. 38. Cobicistat and darunavir increase selpercatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce the selpercatinib dose based on the original dose and monitor for side effects. 39. Darunavir increases sertraline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while also decreasing sertraline levels through an unspecified mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Carefully titrate the SSRI dose based on clinical assessment of antidepressant response. 40. Darunavir increases sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Coadministration with PDE-5 inhibitors may increase the risk of associated adverse reactions, such as hypotension, syncope, visual disturbances, and priapism. 41. Cobicistat and darunavir increase sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 42. Darunavir decreases sitagliptin effects through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 43. Darunavir increases solifenacin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Darunavir increases sorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 45. Darunavir and cobicistat increase sufentanil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, leading to prolonged adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Darunavir increases sunitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 47. Darunavir and cobicistat increase tacrolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 48. Tazemetostat decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 49. Darunavir increases tasimelteon levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised.
